questions.question_text:
An office assistant's gross income for the year is $\$58\,600$ and her allowable tax deductions total $\$1275$.
What is her taxable income, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Added the deductions to the gross income instead of subtracting them.
Ignored the deductions and gave the gross income as the taxable income.
Subtracted the $\$1275$ of deductions twice.

questions.question_text:
A database administrator earned $\$102\,700$ in salary and $\$460$ in bank interest.
He claims $\$1180$ in union fees and $\$2340$ for work-related equipment.
What is his taxable income, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Subtracted only the union fees and left the equipment out of the deductions.
Subtracted the bank interest instead of adding it into the gross income.
Added the deductions to the gross income instead of subtracting them.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=102\,700+460$
$=\$103\,160$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=1180+2340$
$=\$3520$
$\text{Taxable income}=103\,160-3520$
$=\$99\,640$

questions.question_text:
A records clerk's gross income is $\$66\,905.40$ and her allowable tax deductions total $\$1208.75$.
What is her taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar?

options.why: Rounded $\$65\,696.65$ to the nearest dollar instead of rounding it down.
Left the exact amount instead of rounding down to a whole number of dollars.
Added the deductions to the gross income before rounding down.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Taxable income}=66\,905.40-1208.75$
$=65\,696.65$
Rounded down to the nearest whole dollar, the taxable income is $\$65\,696$.

questions.question_text:
An office administrator paid $\$325$ to attend a work-related conference. Her employer reimbursed the full amount.
Why can she not claim this expense as an allowable tax deduction?

options.text: Her employer reimbursed her, so she did not personally bear the expense.
Work-related conference fees can never be claimed.
options.why: Ignored the reimbursement and incorrectly treated every work-related conference fee as non-deductible.

options.text: The expense is too small to be claimed.
options.why: Invented a minimum expense amount instead of applying the condition about reimbursement.

options.text: Only expenses paid through payroll can be claimed.
options.why: Confused deductions from pay with allowable tax deductions for expenses paid personally.

questions.solution_text:
For a work-related expense to be deductible, the taxpayer must have personally incurred it without reimbursement.
Her employer repaid the full $\$325$, so she cannot claim the conference fee.

questions.question_text:
An accounts payable officer's annual tax payable is $\$16\,614$, collected in equal fortnightly PAYG instalments.
What is her fortnightly instalment, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Divided by the $52$ weeks in a year instead of the $26$ fortnights.
Divided by the $12$ months in a year instead of the $26$ fortnights.
Used $13$ four-week periods in the year instead of $26$ fortnights.

questions.question_text:
A payroll assistant's gross weekly pay is $\$1395$ and her weekly PAYG instalment is $\$302.85$.
What is her net weekly pay, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Added the instalment to the gross pay instead of subtracting it.
Treated $\$302.85$ as the annual tax and divided it by $52$ before subtracting.
Subtracted the $\$302.85$ instalment twice.

questions.question_text:
An HR administrator's gross annual income is $\$77\,250$ and her income tax payable is $\$16\,073$.
What is her net income for the year, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Added the tax payable to the gross income instead of subtracting it.
Subtracted the $\$16\,073$ of tax twice.
Divided by $52$ and gave the net weekly pay instead of the net annual income.

questions.question_text:
A finance officer earned a salary of $\$82\,650$ and $\$375$ in bank interest.
His allowable tax deductions are $\$685$ in union fees and $\$1240$ for work-related equipment.
What is his taxable income, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Left the bank interest out of gross income.
Added the $\$1925$ of deductions to gross income instead of subtracting them.
Subtracted only the union fees and omitted the $\$1240$ equipment deduction.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=82\,650+375$
$=\$83\,025$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=685+1240$
$=\$1925$
$\text{Taxable income}=83\,025-1925$
$=\$81\,100$

questions.question_text:
A payroll administrator earns $\$3124.75$ gross per fortnight and received $\$186.60$ in share dividends for the year.
Her allowable tax deductions are $\$9.35$ per week for a work uniform, $\$15.80$ per week in union fees and $\$175$ donated to a registered charity.
What is her annual taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar?

options.why: Multiplied the weekly uniform costs and union fees by $26$ instead of $52$ before rounding down.
Rounded $\$79\,947.30$ up instead of rounding down.
Gave the annual gross income rounded down and did not subtract the allowable deductions.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=3124.75\times26+186.60$
$=81\,243.50+186.60$
$=\$81\,430.10$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=(9.35+15.80)\times52+175$
$=1307.80+175$
$=\$1482.80$
$\text{Taxable income}=81\,430.10-1482.80$
$=79\,947.30$
3. **Round down to the nearest whole dollar**
The taxable income is $\$79\,947$.
